name: Civitas Learning vs. EAB Navigate360
seoTitle: Civitas Learning vs. EAB Navigate360 | Civitas Learning
description: A side-by-side comparison of Civitas Learning and EAB Navigate360 for student success: what each is built to do, how risk is identified, and how impact is measured.
headline: Civitas Learning vs. EAB Navigate360
sub: Both platforms help institutions coordinate student support. They differ on what the prediction is trained on, and on whether the platform can tell you what an initiative changed.
answer: Civitas Learning and EAB Navigate360 are closer than the category talk suggests: both build institution-specific predictive models, both measure intervention impact, and both ship an advising CRM, planning and scheduling tools, and a student mobile app. Two things separate them. The first is deployment: Navigate360 becomes the advising system of record, while Civitas can be your advising CRM or sit beside the one you keep and write back to it, which means the institution decides rather than the vendor. The second is measurement method: EAB compares student lists in its Intervention Effectiveness Tool and publishes retention and graduation ranges, and Civitas builds a matched comparison group from your own records and reports each initiative's lift with its population size and confidence interval.

rows.them: A higher education CRM: advising workflow, case management, campaigns, and a student mobile app. EAB reports more than 850 institutions and over 10 million students, and also sells research and advisory services.
rows.us: A full student success platform and a measurement layer: an advising CRM with case management, notes, alerts, and outreach, collaborative degree planning, registration, class scheduling, and a student mobile app, on one unified dataset with institution-specific models. Deploy it as your advising system of record, or beside the one you already run.

rows.them: Custom predictive models built per institution, on as much as ten years of student information system history plus optional LMS data. EAB reports more than 200 custom-built models deployed. It does not publish a refresh cadence or an accuracy figure.
rows.us: A model trained on your own SIS, LMS, CRM, and aid history, weighing grades, credits, course patterns, aid status, and engagement together, retrained every term, at 89% accuracy on student outcomes, with the driving factors shown for each prediction.

rows.them: An Intervention Effectiveness Tool that compares student lists on metrics such as persistence. EAB publishes graduation gains of 3% to 15%, retention gains of 2% to 12%, and a typical 5:1 return, without publishing the matching method or a confidence interval.
rows.us: Lift against a matched comparison group of your own students, with the population size and the confidence interval reported for each initiative. Across 220 measured initiatives, 40–60% produced a measurable outcome, and the ones that did not are reported too.

rows.them: Navigate360 AI adds pre-built agents for enrollment and retention, a 24/7 student assistant, natural-language reporting, and grade and LMS alert monitoring. EAB reports an average staff capacity increase above 25%.
rows.us: Agents act on your institution's own model rather than a vendor model, every action is logged and attributed, and there is no token metering and no charge per agent.

rows.them: Primarily inside Navigate360, which becomes the advising system of record for many institutions.
rows.us: Your choice, and that is the point. Civitas can be the advising system of record, or it can sit beside your existing CRM and case management tool and write actions and results back to them. Nothing has to be replaced, and nothing stops you replacing it.

rows.them: Focused on student success, advising, and the student experience, with a strong student-facing mobile app.
rows.us: The whole institution: enrollment, engagement, persistence, completion, career outcomes, course demand, and program accountability on one dataset, with the advising tools on top of it rather than beside it.

rows.them: A mature student mobile app for scheduling, to-dos, and communication.
rows.us: Collaborative degree planning, the smart class schedule builder, registration, appointment scheduling, asynchronous guidance, and a student mobile app.

rows.them: EAB also sells research and advisory services with benchmarking and best-practice publications. Whether any of it is included with the platform is a contract question to put to them.
rows.us: A Customer Development team that works on your own numbers, plus the annual Student Success Impact Report drawn from measured partner initiatives.

themBest: You want one packaged system that becomes the advising system of record and you have no reason to keep the tools you own.
You want the platform and a research and advisory relationship from one company.
Scale of installed base matters to your committee: EAB reports more than 850 institutions.
usBest: You have to show a board, a system office, or an accreditor which initiatives produced a measured outcome, and which did not.
You already own a CRM, an early alert tool, or an AI agent platform, and replacing them is not on the table.
The question is institutional, not only advising: enrollment, course demand, completion, program accountability, and graduate earnings on the same dataset.
You need predictions trained on your own students rather than on sector patterns, refreshed every term.

faqs.q: Is Civitas Learning a replacement for EAB Navigate360?
faqs.a: It can be, and that is the difference worth understanding. Civitas ships the advising CRM, case management, planning, registration, scheduling, and a student mobile app, so it can replace Navigate360 outright. It can also sit beside a tool you would rather keep and write back to it. Navigate360 generally expects advising work to move into Navigate360.

faqs.q: What is the main difference between Civitas Learning and EAB Navigate360?
faqs.a: Both measure, so the difference is the method and what gets published with the number. EAB's Intervention Effectiveness Tool compares student lists, and EAB publishes retention and graduation ranges; Civitas builds a matched comparison group from your own records and reports each initiative's lift with its confidence interval and population size. Ask both vendors how the comparison group is built and whether you are given the interval.

faqs.q: Which one has better predictive analytics?
faqs.a: Both build institution-specific models. EAB reports more than 200 custom models deployed, some on ten years of history. The questions that separate the two are how often the model is refreshed and whether the vendor publishes an accuracy figure your institutional research office can audit: Civitas retrains each term and publishes 89% accuracy on student outcomes.

faqs.q: Can we run both?
faqs.a: Yes. Civitas integrates with more than 100 systems and does not require you to give up an existing advising or case management tool, so institutions mid-contract often keep Navigate360 and add Civitas for the model and the efficacy measurement, then decide at renewal whether to consolidate.

faqs.q: How should we evaluate the two?
faqs.a: Ask each vendor for a lift number against a comparison group, the size of that group, and the confidence interval, then ask them to name an intervention of theirs that did not work. The ten-question vendor checklist →

name: Civitas Learning vs. Salesforce Education Cloud
seoTitle: Civitas Learning vs. Salesforce Education Cloud | Civitas Learning
description: How Civitas Learning and Salesforce Education Cloud differ: a CRM platform you configure versus a measurement layer with institution-specific predictive models. They are frequently run together.
headline: Civitas Learning vs. Salesforce Education Cloud
sub: These two are not the same kind of product, and most institutions that ask the question end up running both.
answer: Salesforce Education Cloud is a configurable CRM platform an institution builds on; Civitas Learning is a measurement layer that unifies data from the systems an institution already runs, predicts outcomes with institution-specific models, and measures what each initiative changed. Education Cloud ships an education data model with grades and courses as native objects, Agentforce agents, and predictive insights, and Salesforce is building a next-generation student information system on it. Civitas arrives with the higher education data model, the models, and the comparison-group measurement already built and maintained. Civitas integrates with Salesforce, so the common outcome is not a choice between them: the CRM stays the system of record for relationships, and Civitas supplies the prediction and the proof.

rows.them: A configurable CRM platform for higher education, with education-specific objects such as grades and courses, Agentforce agents, and a large partner and app ecosystem.
rows.us: A purpose-built measurement layer for higher education: unified data, institution-specific predictive models, action in existing workflows, and comparison-group measurement.

rows.them: Salesforce does not publish an implementation timeline. It depends on how much you configure and who does the work, so ask for a date with your own requirements attached.
rows.us: Lawrence Technological University was live in six weeks. The higher education data model and the predictive models are not built from scratch per customer.

rows.them: Agentforce for Education provides pre-built agent skills and predictive insights on the Salesforce record. Salesforce does not publish a model accuracy figure or a refresh cadence.
rows.us: Models trained on the institution's whole record across the SIS, LMS, CRM, and aid systems, retrained each term, at 89% accuracy on student outcomes.

rows.them: Pre-built analytics and AI predictions on the Salesforce record, plus whatever reporting you build. No published comparison-group efficacy method.
rows.us: Lift per initiative against a matched comparison group, with a confidence interval, out of the box.

rows.them: Strongest on the Salesforce record, which now holds grades and courses natively, and Salesforce is building a next-generation SIS on Education Cloud.
rows.us: More than 100 systems, including the SIS, LMS, financial aid, HR, finance, engagement tools, and the campus card system.

rows.them: The institution, usually with an administrator and often an implementation partner.
rows.us: Civitas maintains the integrations and the models as part of the subscription.

rows.them: Salesforce is one of the CRMs Civitas reads from and writes back to.
rows.us: Civitas does not require you to replace the CRM: scores and actions land in Salesforce where your staff already work. Where you would rather not build advising in Salesforce, Civitas provides the advising CRM, planning, registration, and scheduling itself.

themBest: Salesforce is already an institutional standard and you want the student lifecycle on the same platform as everything else.
You need deep process customization and you have the administrator capacity or partner budget to build and maintain it.
The requirement is relationship and process management, such as recruitment, advancement, or service desks, rather than outcome measurement.
You are interested in consolidating on one vendor as Salesforce extends Education Cloud toward a student information system.
usBest: You need predictions and efficacy measurement without a multi-quarter build.
The data that predicts persistence lives outside the CRM, in the SIS, the LMS, and the aid system.
You want the higher education data model, the definitions, and the comparison-group method already built and maintained.
You are being asked to prove return on investment, not to report on pipeline.

faqs.q: Does Civitas Learning replace Salesforce?
faqs.a: It does not have to. Salesforce is one of the CRMs Civitas reads from and writes back to, alongside Slate, Element451, CollegeVine, and TargetX, and many institutions keep it as the system of record for relationships. For advising specifically, Civitas ships its own CRM, case management, planning, registration, and scheduling, so institutions that do not want to build all of that in Salesforce do not have to.

faqs.q: Can we just build this in Salesforce ourselves?
faqs.a: Salesforce ships an education data model and predictive insights, so this is not a build-from-nothing question. The parts institutions most often underestimate are joining the record across systems that are not the CRM, keeping an institution-specific model retrained every term, and constructing a defensible comparison group per initiative.

faqs.q: We already own Salesforce. Is Civitas redundant?
faqs.a: No, and the overlap is smaller than it looks. Salesforce holds the interactions; Civitas predicts the outcome from the whole record across every system and measures whether the interaction changed it. Where the two do overlap, on advising workflow, you choose which one your advisors work in.

faqs.q: Which is faster to implement?
faqs.a: Civitas is generally faster, because the higher education data model and the predictive models are not built per customer: Lawrence Technological University went live in six weeks. Salesforce does not publish an implementation timeline, so ask for one against your own requirements rather than taking a range from either of us.

faqs.q: How do we compare the two on cost?
faqs.a: Compare the total: platform licenses plus implementation plus the administrator or integrator time to build and maintain what you need. Civitas is an annual subscription that includes integration, model build, and the partnership. How Civitas pricing works →

name: Civitas Learning vs. Element451
seoTitle: Civitas Learning vs. Element451 | Civitas Learning
description: How Civitas Learning and Element451 differ: an AI-native CRM built for the front door versus a measurement layer that proves which initiatives changed persistence and completion.
headline: Civitas Learning vs. Element451
sub: One is built to run the front door. One is built to prove what the work produced. They integrate.
answer: Element451 is an AI-native CRM with the deepest history at the front door — marketing, admissions, inquiry response, and the enrollment funnel — and it now sells student success and retention products as well, reading SIS and LMS data to monitor grades and engagement. Civitas Learning is a measurement layer across the whole institution, with predictive models trained on each institution's own history and lift reported against a matched comparison group. Both publish outcome numbers, so the difference to test is the method behind them: Element451 publishes a 2–7% term-to-term retention lift without publishing a comparison method, and Civitas publishes the population size and the confidence interval for each initiative. Element451 is one of the CRMs Civitas reads from, so institutions frequently run both.

rows.them: Deepest at the front door — marketing, admissions, inquiry response, and the enrollment funnel — with AI agents handling conversation at volume, and student success and retention products added to that.
rows.us: The whole student lifecycle and the institution behind it: enroll, engage, persist, graduate, employ, and prove.

rows.dimension: What the AI is trained on
rows.them: Element451 does not publish what its models are trained on. That is a question to put to them directly, and the answer is worth having in writing.
rows.us: A model trained per institution on that institution's own SIS, LMS, CRM, and aid history, retrained each term, at 89% accuracy.

rows.them: Element451 publishes a 2–7% lift in term-to-term retention and 3–10% grade gains when alerts trigger timely intervention, alongside activity and efficiency measures. It does not publish the comparison method or a confidence interval.
rows.us: Lift against a matched comparison group of your own students, with the population size and the confidence interval, per initiative, including the initiatives that produced nothing.

rows.them: A public price calculator returns a real annual figure before you speak to anyone, followed by a formal quote. That genuinely lowers buyer risk early.
rows.us: An annual subscription scaled to institution size, with no token metering and no per-agent charge. No published list price.

rows.them: A CRM: for many institutions it becomes the system of record for recruitment and communication.
rows.us: Reads from more than 100 systems, including Element451, and writes actions and results back. Where you want it to, Civitas is also the advising CRM itself. Nothing has to be replaced, and nothing stops you replacing it.

rows.them: Enrollment and student engagement, extending into student success. Element451 reads SIS and LMS data, including Banner, Colleague, Canvas, and Blackboard, and monitors grades and engagement.
rows.us: Also course demand, program portfolio, aid leverage, institutional research, and graduate earnings against the federal earnings test.

themBest: The problem you are solving is at the front door: inquiry volume, response time, application completion, and yield communication.
You are replacing or consolidating a CRM and want AI agents native to it.
You want a real price before you talk to a salesperson. Their public calculator gives you one.
usBest: The question is whether an initiative worked, and you need a number a board or an accreditor will accept.
You are keeping the CRM you have, including Element451, and need prediction and measurement across every other system too.
Retention, completion, and program accountability matter as much as the funnel.
You need models trained on your own students, not on the sector.

faqs.q: Do Civitas Learning and Element451 compete?
faqs.a: They overlap more than they used to. Element451 began at the front door and now sells student success and retention products that read SIS and LMS data; Civitas ships an advising CRM, planning, registration, and scheduling alongside its measurement layer. The practical difference is that Element451 is the CRM, and Civitas can either be the CRM or read from the one you run. Element451 is a supported integration.

faqs.q: Can we use both?
faqs.a: Yes, and institutions do. Element451 runs the recruitment and engagement communication and raises its own alerts; Civitas supplies the institution-specific model across every system and the comparison-group measurement that says whether any of it changed an outcome.

faqs.q: Which has better AI?
faqs.a: That depends on the job, and on what each vendor will tell you about the model. For conversation at volume at the front door, an AI-native CRM is built for it. For predicting which enrolled student will not return next term, ask what the model was trained on and how often it is refreshed: Civitas trains per institution and retrains each term, and Element451 does not publish an answer.

faqs.q: Why does Civitas not publish a price when Element451 does?
faqs.a: Because the number depends on institution size, scope, and how many systems are integrated. Published tiers are genuinely useful to a buyer, and the honest answer is that we will give you a quote against your own headcount and system list in the first conversation. How pricing works →

faqs.q: How do we compare them fairly?
faqs.a: Ask both for the same evidence: a lift number against a comparison group, the group size, the confidence interval, and an intervention of theirs that did not work. The ten-question vendor checklist →

name: Student success platform alternatives
seoTitle: Student Success Platform Alternatives: How to Compare | Civitas Learning
description: The categories of student success software, what each is built for, and the six questions that separate them. A buyer's guide for provosts, VPs of student success, and IR leaders.
headline: Student success platform alternatives, and how to tell them apart
sub: Four kinds of product get sold as a student success platform. They solve different problems, and the demos look alike.
answer: There are four categories of student success software, and the fastest way to tell them apart is to ask what each one produces as proof, and whether it makes you move your work into it. Student success management systems produce advising activity and expect advising to live in them. AI-native CRMs produce engagement and efficiency and are the CRM. Data warehouses and business intelligence tools produce reports. Measurement platforms such as Civitas Learning produce lift against a matched comparison group, and ship the advising, planning, and scheduling tools too, so the institution decides whether to keep its CRM or use theirs. Most institutions need more than one category, and the mistake is buying two products from the same one and expecting different answers.

rows.them: Advising workflow, case management, campaigns, a student app, and intervention reporting. Examples include EAB Navigate360.
rows.us: Buy it when advising work should live in one packaged system. Ask how the intervention comparison is constructed, and whether you get a confidence interval with the number.

rows.them: Conversational agents, recruitment and engagement communication at volume, extending into student success. Examples include Element451 and CollegeVine.
rows.us: Buy it for the front door. Ask what the model is trained on and how often it is refreshed, and ask for the method behind any retention number they publish.

rows.them: Configurable relationship and process management across the lifecycle. Examples include Salesforce Education Cloud and Slate.
rows.us: Buy it when you need process flexibility and have the capacity to build and maintain it. Budget for the implementation, not just the license.

rows.them: Storage, joins, and dashboards over institutional data.
rows.us: Buy it if you have the engineering capacity to build and maintain the higher education data model. It stores and displays; it does not predict or measure.

rows.them: Institution-specific predictive models and comparison-group efficacy measurement, with advising, planning, and scheduling tools on the same dataset. This is what Civitas Learning is.
rows.us: Buy it when you have to prove which initiatives moved persistence, completion, or revenue, and defend the number. It is also the only option in this list that lets you keep your CRM or use its own.

themBest: You need a single packaged system for advising, and measurement is not the reason you are buying.
The urgent problem is at the front door, and enrollment communication is the bottleneck.
You have the engineering capacity to build and maintain your own data model and analytics.
usBest: Performance-based funding, a board, or an accreditor is asking which initiatives worked.
You want to decide for yourself whether to keep your CRM or consolidate onto one platform, rather than have the vendor decide.
You need one dataset that answers enrollment, engagement, persistence, completion, and career outcome questions the same way.
You want the prediction trained on your own students, refreshed each term.

faqs.q: What are the main alternatives to Civitas Learning?
faqs.a: The most common alternatives fall into four categories: student success management systems such as EAB Navigate360, AI-native CRMs such as Element451 and CollegeVine, CRM platforms such as Salesforce Education Cloud and Slate, and in-house data warehouse and business intelligence builds. Each answers a different question, and only some of them measure whether an initiative worked.

faqs.q: How do I compare student success platforms fairly?
faqs.a: Ask every vendor the same six questions: what the model is trained on, how often it is refreshed, how the comparison group behind any outcome claim is built, whether you get the population size and the confidence interval, which of your systems they replace, and how long until an advisor sees a prediction about a real student. Most vendors now publish an outcome number, so the method behind it is what separates them. The full ten-question checklist →

faqs.q: Can one platform do all of it?
faqs.a: Not usually, and a vendor claiming otherwise is worth a second look. The practical pattern is a system of record for relationships, a system for the advising workflow, and a measurement layer that reads across both.

faqs.q: What should we do first?
faqs.a: Write down the question you have to answer, and who is asking it. A board asking about return on investment, a provost asking which programs are at risk under the federal earnings rule, and a VP asking how to staff advising are three different purchases.

faqs.q: How much should we expect to spend?
faqs.a: Compare the total cost, including implementation and the internal capacity to maintain it, rather than the license alone. How Civitas pricing works →
